passage: Class 5 teacher's note, results day. Kavitha topped the class in the term exams and glowed all morning; twice I heard her tell the row in front what her total was. Then she noticed Ayesha folding a paper into a small square, and Kavitha stopped mid-sentence. At lunch she asked Ayesha to show her how to shade maps so neatly, and admitted her own map marks were her lowest. When I congratulated her, I said there was nothing wrong with feeling glad. She answered, "I'm really happy, but I don't want to be loud about it." I will see how she handles the next round of results. 🙂

qa.q: How many times did the teacher hear Kavitha tell the row in front what her total was?
qa.a: Twice; the teacher heard her tell the row in front what her total was.

qa.q: What was Kavitha feeling when she noticed Ayesha folding the paper, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Pride mixed with sudden thoughtfulness: she stopped mid-sentence and then asked Ayesha for help, saying she was happy but did not want to be loud.

qa.q: What would you advise Kavitha to do the next time results come out?
qa.a: Enjoy being glad, share the news quietly, and keep remembering what classmates like Ayesha are good at.

qa.q: How might Ayesha have felt when Kavitha asked for help with the maps?
qa.a: Ayesha may have felt noticed for a real strength after a disappointing morning, though it could also have stung a little; the note does not say.

grounding: Illustrates a top scorer feeling proud and choosing modest sharing while valuing a friend's strength.

passage: Thursday, after dinner. Maths test came back. I got 14 out of 25 and I was hoping for at least 20. On the bus I kept thinking, I must be stupid 😔. Nitin sat next to me and said he lost marks on fractions too, and I didn't say anything. At home I looked at my paper again. All the fraction word problems are wrong, but the multiplication ones are almost all right. That's not everything, is it? Tomorrow I'll ask Papa to give me five fraction sums to do before school. Maybe Nitin can do them with me. - Varun

qa.q: What score did Varun get in the maths test?
qa.a: Varun got 14 out of 25.

qa.q: What does Varun think on the bus, and what raises doubt about it at home?
qa.a: On the bus Varun thinks "I must be stupid"; at home Varun sees the multiplication answers are almost all right, which raises the question whether one weak topic is everything.

qa.q: What small step would help Varun with fractions?
qa.a: Doing a few fraction sums each day, as Varun plans to ask Papa for, and checking which fraction problems went wrong 🙂.

qa.q: How might Nitin see Varun's silence on the bus?
qa.a: Nitin, who also lost marks on fractions, may have thought Varun was upset and just wanted company; he may not have known how badly Varun felt.

grounding: Illustrates a child doubting themselves after a low mark and shifting to asking which topic went wrong and how to practise.

passage: The maths tests were handed back before lunch at the school in Melbourne. Soo-ah slid hers into her bag without looking at the mark again, jaw tight. Her desk partner Leila whispered, "How did you go?" and Soo-ah only shrugged. Before the bell, the teacher crouched by her desk and said quietly, "I've seen how many afternoons you stayed back to redo those problems. Your effort is showing in your working, even if not yet in the mark." Soo-ah's shoulders came down. At lunch she took out her sandwich, told Leila the score, and asked if Leila would check her working on question six.

qa.q: Where did the teacher crouch to speak with Soo-ah?
qa.a: The teacher crouched by her desk.

qa.q: What does Soo-ah's change of posture suggest she felt after the teacher spoke?
qa.a: Her shoulders came down, which suggests relief and a feeling of being seen; later she shared her score and asked Leila for help, so she seemed steadier 🙂.

qa.q: How could a teacher support a student with low marks on results day?
qa.a: Quietly point to specific effort, like staying back to redo problems, so the student knows someone has noticed and believes in them.

qa.q: How might Leila have seen Soo-ah's shrug, and then the lunchtime request?
qa.a: Leila may have wondered whether to ask again, and probably felt trusted when Soo-ah shared the score and asked for help.

grounding: Illustrates a child with low marks steadied by a teacher who names her effort.

passage: Teacher's note, Grade 6 spelling test. Baljeet leaned across the aisle and whispered to Lokesh, "Let me see what you wrote, Lokesh. We're friends, aren't we?" I was two desks away and heard it. Lokesh's ears went red and he moved his arm over his sheet. "I can't. We'll both get into trouble," he said, barely audible. Baljeet sat back in his chair with a scowl. At recess I saw them on the bench, Lokesh holding the word list and testing Baljeet on the tricky ones. Later Lokesh told me he had hated that moment because he did not want to lose his friend. I did not need to step in, and I told him so.

qa.q: Where did Lokesh and Baljeet sit at recess?
qa.a: They sat on the bench, with Lokesh holding the word list.

qa.q: What was Lokesh worried about when he refused?
qa.a: He was worried about both of them getting into trouble, and about losing his friend; he told the teacher he hated that moment because he did not want to lose his friend.

qa.q: What would you advise Lokesh if Baljeet asks again?
qa.a: He can keep saying no kindly and repeat his offer to practise the words together, since a real friend would not want him to risk trouble.

qa.q: How might Baljeet have felt when Lokesh refused?
qa.a: Baljeet may have felt embarrassed or annoyed, as the scowl suggests, yet still sat with Lokesh at recess, so he may also have been glad of the help.

grounding: Illustrates a child pressed by a friend to share answers, feeling torn, refusing and offering to help him study.

passage: Note from the class teacher, after the science test. Payal stayed at her desk when the others left and asked to speak to me. She said that during question 7 she had seen Vandana's answer from where she sat, and no one was looking. "I wanted those marks so much," she said. "But then I thought, if I write that, the answer isn't mine." She had written her own answer, unsure and probably wrong. She still looked a little sorry about the lost mark. I told her I was glad she came to talk, and we agreed on a short revision plan for the unit on electricity. She left with a lighter step.

qa.q: During which question did Payal see Vandana's answer?
qa.a: She saw it during question 7.

qa.q: What did Payal want, and what did she worry about, while she looked at question 7?
qa.a: She wanted the marks, but she also wanted the answer to be her own; afterwards she still looked a little sorry about the lost mark.

qa.q: What small step would help Payal with the unit on electricity?
qa.a: A short revision plan with the teacher, so that her own answers get stronger.

qa.q: How might Vandana feel if Vandana later heard what Payal did?
qa.a: Vandana might be surprised and maybe respect Payal for it; the note does not say Vandana ever found out.

grounding: Illustrates a child tempted by a friend's visible answer who chooses to write her own.

passage: The corridor outside the staffroom smelled of chalk and floor polish. Himani stood holding her returned science quiz, a big red 10 out of 10 at the top, and stared at it. "You got the highest and you look like you swallowed a lemon," said Pallavi, joining her. Himani lowered her voice. "The last two answers weren't mine. I copied them from the girl in front. Nobody saw." Her stomach had been tight since Monday. "Then why does it still feel bad?" Pallavi asked. Himani took a breath and knocked on the staffroom door. "I'm going to tell Ma'am," she said, "and I'm not doing it again."

qa.q: Where did Himani copy the last two answers from?
qa.a: She copied them from the girl in front.

qa.q: What does Himani's tight stomach suggest she feels about the copied answers?
qa.a: It suggests she feels uneasy and guilty; it has bothered her since Monday even though nobody saw and the mark is high.

qa.q: What could Himani do that is better than pretending nothing happened?
qa.a: Own up to the teacher and decide not to copy again, which is what she is about to do.

qa.q: How might Pallavi see Himani's decision?
qa.a: Pallavi may be surprised and a little worried for Himani, but may also respect her honesty, since Pallavi was the one who asked why it still felt bad.

grounding: Illustrates a child uneasy after copying once who chooses to admit it and not repeat it.

passage: Wasim's eyes slid to the right before he could stop them. Devika's answer to question 4 sat there in neat handwriting. The ceiling fan clicked over the Grade 6 classroom in Nagpur, and then the teacher's footsteps came down the aisle. Wasim's heart thumped and he snapped his eyes back to his own page. "I'm only scared because the teacher is coming," he thought. "If they left the room right now, would I look again?" The teacher tapped a desk to check a pencil box and moved on. Wasim wrote what he could remember, half sure it was wrong, and felt his shoulders drop.

qa.q: In which city is Wasim's classroom?
qa.a: It is in Nagpur.

qa.q: What is Wasim afraid of when he hears the footsteps, and what question does he ask himself?
qa.a: He is afraid of being caught glancing at Devika's paper, and he asks himself whether he would look again if the teacher left the room.

qa.q: What could Wasim try next time he is tempted during a test?
qa.a: He can ask himself what he would do if nobody ever found out, and keep his eyes on his own page and write what he remembers.

qa.q: How might the teacher see that moment in the aisle?
qa.a: The teacher was probably just checking the room, tapping a desk to look at a pencil box; a glance alone does not tell them what a student is thinking.

grounding: Illustrates a child afraid of being caught glancing at another paper and asking whether it is honesty or only fear.

passage: Irawati lay on her bed in the third-floor flat. In the hall, her father Asif was telling his brother on the phone that she would "take first rank again this year." She had come second last time. Her pencil box sat on the desk and a small ugly thought came: what if she made sure of first rank some other way? Her throat felt tight. She wiped her face, walked into the hall and said, "Papa, when you say first rank every day, I get scared. I don't want to come second." Asif put down the phone. "I didn't know it felt that heavy," he said, and sat beside her.

qa.q: Who was Asif talking to on the phone?
qa.a: He was talking to his brother.

qa.q: What was Irawati feeling when the thought of making sure of first rank some other way came?
qa.a: She was frightened of coming second and disappointing her father; her tight throat and wiped face suggest she felt overwhelmed.

qa.q: What did Irawati do that worked, and why?
qa.a: She told Asif honestly how heavy the pressure felt, which opened a talk instead of leaving her alone with the idea; a lower honest score is safer than a high dishonest one 🙂.

qa.q: What is it like for Asif to hear this from Irawati?
qa.a: He seems surprised and concerned: he put down the phone and said he had not known it felt that heavy, so he may now be ready to listen.

grounding: Illustrates a child under parental demand for top rank who honestly tells her father the pressure instead of cheating.

passage: Monday. At lunch Tarun told the whole bench that Anand had copied in the maths test. "He's a cheat," he said loudly, and three kids gasped. Wednesday. Anand ate alone by the water cooler and nobody talked to him. Tarun was still angry, but a friend asked, "So everyone knows now. Did anything change?" Tarun had no answer. Friday. Before the first bell, Tarun went to the teacher's table and said quietly what he had seen, and that he had already told others, which he now wished he hadn't. "Thank you, I'll look into it," the teacher said. Tarun walked back lighter, though unsure Anand would forgive how he'd talked.

qa.q: What did Tarun do on Friday before the first bell?
qa.a: On Friday Tarun went to the teacher's table and said quietly what he had seen.

qa.q: Why might Tarun have felt lighter on Friday but still unsure?
qa.a: He had dealt with the real problem by telling the teacher, but he regretted how he had talked earlier and worried Anand might not forgive it.

qa.q: What went wrong on Monday, and what fixed it?
qa.a: Telling the bench loudly spread the story but changed nothing except leaving Anand alone; quietly telling the teacher on Friday put it with someone who can act.

qa.q: How was Wednesday for Anand?
qa.a: Anand ate alone by the water cooler and nobody talked to him, so he was probably feeling isolated and ashamed.

grounding: Illustrates a classmate's contempt and gossip about a cheater turning into a quiet report to the teacher.

passage: My name is Kavitha, and last month Ayaan sat with me for an hour in the colony park and explained my Hindi homework until I finally understood it. I was so grateful. So when our unit test came and Ayaan whispered, "Remember what I did? Show me your answers," my stomach dropped. I did owe Ayaan something, that was true. But copying would put us both in trouble. I said, "I can't do that. But come to my house after school and I'll go through the chapter with you, like you did for me." Ayaan was a bit sulky, but he came over on Saturday. We spent the afternoon on the chapter, and by the end the sulking was gone.

qa.q: Where did Ayaan help Kavitha with the Hindi homework?
qa.a: Ayaan helped Kavitha in the colony park.

qa.q: What was Kavitha feeling when Ayaan whispered the request?
qa.a: Kavitha's stomach dropped: Kavitha felt pulled between gratitude for the help and knowing that copying would put both of them in trouble.

qa.q: How could Kavitha repay a friend who once helped?
qa.a: Kavitha could keep offering to study together, like going through the chapter after school.

qa.q: How might Ayaan have seen Kavitha's refusal?
qa.a: At first perhaps let down, as the sulky reaction shows, but the offer to study together may have shown that Kavitha still valued the friendship.

grounding: Illustrates a child who is grateful to a friend yet refuses to help him cheat and repays honestly.
